name_reason: Current name is convention-compliant (data_fd2_<domain=animation>_<descriptor>), free of Ghidra address residue, reflects a table type, and is symmetric with its two sibling tables (data_fd2_animation_spell_sprite_offset_table @0x51F33, data_fd2_animation_spell_frame_count_table @0x51F54). One minor imprecision: each element is the sound-effect id passed to fd2_play_sfx_with_handle, not a frame number; the '_sfx_frame_' descriptor conflates the SFX id with the frame-0 trigger. A tighter name would be data_fd2_animation_spell_sfx_id_table (or _frame0_sfx_id_table). Left uncertain rather than rename: the descriptor is not wrong (values drive the frame-0 SFX hook), there is no convention violation, and a Stage-2 rename (protos.h/globals.h + 2 call-site files) is hard to justify for a cosmetic precision tweak that also breaks the clean 3-table naming symmetry. Stage 2 to decide.
stage2_review: rename -> data_fd2_animation_spell_sfx_id_table. Reverses the shard's keep lean: live decomp of the sole reader fd2_animate_spell_impact_per_target shows table[spell_id] value is passed directly as the sfx-id arg to fd2_play_sfx_with_handle (same arg slot as the special-case SFX consts 3/5/7/8/0xA/0xF), and the trigger frame is fixed at 0. So the value is an SFX id, not a frame index -- '_frame_' is a semantic error, not cosmetic. Stage 2 must also correct the Ghidra plate (currently 'SFX trigger frame index'). Symmetry with sprite_offset/frame_count siblings is preserved (all name the value).
purpose: Per-spell primary SFX id for the per-target spell-impact animation; element value is the sound-effect id fired on frame 0 of that spell's impact effect (0 = no frame-0 SFX hook).
logic_summary: Third of three parallel per-spell byte tables consumed by fd2_animate_spell_impact_per_target (@0x1C4CC; the snapshot copy + frame-0 read are the two xrefs at 0x1C50D/0x1C512). The reader copies all 33 bytes into a stack scratch (8-dword REP MOVSD + tail MOVSB). On frame_idx==0 it tests tmp[spell_id] != 0 and, if set, calls fd2_play_sfx_with_handle(handle, tmp[spell_id], 1). Additional per-frame SFX cues for specific spells (0x16/0x19/0x12/0x13/0x08/0x09 on particular frames) come from an inline dispatch chain in the reader, not from this table. Sibling tables: _sprite_offset_table @0x51F33 (sprite-base offset), _frame_count_table @0x51F54 (outer frame-loop bound).
element_semantics: One byte per spell_id (index 0..32). Each byte is the SFX id played on frame 0 of that spell's per-target impact animation; 0 means no frame-0 SFX hook. Verified content (33 bytes): {6,6,6,6,9,9,9,9,10,14,0,0,0,12,12,12,12,6,7,8,4,4,3,0,0,5,3,2,0,0,0,0,9}, byte-identical to the Ghidra image at 0x51F75 and to the src initializer.
notes: Datatype byte[33] in Ghidra matches src const uint8[33] and the 33-byte REP-MOVSD+MOVSB copy extent (next table _overlay_blink_mask_table begins at 0x52006, but the immediately-adjacent bytes at +33 are still part of the sibling-table region; the 33-byte extent is fixed by the copy width). xrefs: 1 READ + 1 DATA, both from fd2_animate_spell_impact_per_target; zero writers -> const confirmed. A second consumer mirror exists in the rebuilt source (src/anim/anicombt.c fd2_animate_spell_impact_per_target) which memcpy's the same 33 bytes and reads sfx_frame_tbl[spell_id]; semantics match the Ghidra reader. Ghidra PLATE_COMMENT was null; created a concise plate (len 1102) from the src conclusions. No src edit (comment kept); only this shard is staged.
